extracted.intended_audience: writers and critics of comic fiction and literary essays
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for comic/witty writing and literary criticism, emphasizing the relation between humor, sentiment, sincerity, and seriousness in fiction and essays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sense of an unuttered joy
rubrics_metrics.description: This new frivolity is inadequate because there is in it no strong sense of an unuttered joy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective comedy should convey an underlying, unspoken joy in the characters — repartee and nonsense must spring from merriment, not emptiness of heart. When talk is lively it must feel light-hearted, not merely light-headed; even nonsense should be abundant and generous rather than 'precious nonsense.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Humour rooted in sentimental courage
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief cause of modern incapacity is the miserable fear of being sentimental... There has been no humour so robust or uproarious as that of the sentimentalist Steele or Sterne or Dickens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Robust comedy often arises from writers willing to be sentimental — even 'silly sentimentalism.' One must have the courage to 'write so badly' when necessary; that innocence and largeness of scale produce both powerful pathos and strong humour. Anti-pattern: avoiding all sentimentality in the name of taste produces frigid, feeble wits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Touch the heart to produce a hearty laugh
rubrics_metrics.description: For a hearty laugh it is necessary to have touched the heart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedy that truly moves requires connection with primary emotions — joy, triumph, amusement — not merely mockery or detached cleverness. To write such comedy one needs friendship, honour, abysmal tenderness and openness (as exemplified by Dr. Johnson).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid chronic pessimism in comic tone
rubrics_metrics.description: All our comedians are tragic comedians... These later fashionable writers are so pessimistic in bone and marrow that they never seem able to imagine the heart having any concern with mirth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers should not let pervasive pessimism or tragic outlook dominate their comic voice; imagine the heart capable of mirth. Anti-pattern: repartee produced from self-hatred, bankruptcy, or despair — joking because one is not merry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open, indecent humanity and confession of primary pities
rubrics_metrics.description: Above all, it is necessary to be openly and indecently humane, to confess with fulness all the primary pities and fears of Adam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sincerity and humane warmth (fear of death, tenderness) give depth to both serious and comic writing. Being candid about vulnerabilities makes the humour honest and the serious passages credible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portrayal of emotion over idealized repression
rubrics_metrics.description: This ideal of self-repression... is, whatever else it is, not English... From representing aristocrats as people who suppressed their feelings, it has been an easy step to representing aristocrats as people who had no feelings to suppress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid valorizing stoical repression or depicting characters (especially aristocrats) as inherently heartless. Authentic portrayals should show feeling and emotional display; the living tradition of English letters has been emotional and sentimental rather than mute stoicism.

rubrics_metrics.name: License to joke about serious subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: All jesting is in its nature profane... If a joke is not a joke about religion or morals, it is a joke about police-magistrates or scientific professors... To take a thing and make a joke out of it is not to take it in vain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humour addressing religion, morals, or other solemn topics is legitimate and can be deeply useful — jokes may reveal truths and energize belief. Anti-pattern: equating solemnity with respectability and condemning all levity on sacred topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paradox and the unexpected as serious methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Paradox simply means a certain defiant joy which belongs to belief... The only serious reason which I can imagine inducing any one person to listen to any other is, that the first person looks to the second person with an ardent faith and a fixed attention, expecting him to say what he does not expect him to say.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use paradox, surprise, and unexpected formulations as legitimate, even necessary, rhetorical methods in philosophical and persuasive writing. Originality and the 'unexpected' are key to holding attention and conveying belief. Anti-pattern: demanding only stately, expected, 'serious' prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solemnity is not proof of sincerity
rubrics_metrics.description: In the modern world solemnity is the direct enemy of sincerity... The thing which is fundamentally and really frivolous is a careless solemnity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not conflate verbosity and momentous tones with authenticity. Prefer lively, sincere expression (even if comic) to inflated solemn rhetoric that can be empty or frivolous in effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art should be participatory, not merely specialist spectacle
rubrics_metrics.description: The ballets of the Alhambra are institutions in which a particular selected row of persons in pink go through an operation known as dancing... A person could dance without being a dancer; a person could dance without being a specialist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultural practices and art-forms are healthiest when accessible and practised by ordinary people rather than confined to trained specialists. Anti-pattern: professionalization that turns common joy (dancing, laughing) into a hired spectacle; correspondingly avoid making art only for connoisseurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infuse writing with riotous joy and festivity
rubrics_metrics.description: If he objects to my treating of life riotously, I reply that life is a riot... the Universe as I see it, at any rate, is very much more like the fireworks at the Crystal Palace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a tone that recognizes life's 'tense and secret festivity' — energetic, celebratory, and exuberant imagination can be a legitimate stance toward cosmic and human matters. Anti-pattern: dour, monochrome solemnity that denies celebration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral sympathy matters in art and criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: The doctrine of the distinction between art and morality owes a great part of its success to art and morality being hopelessly mixed up in the persons and performances of its greatest exponents... If he really wished us to believe that he cared for beauty only, he ought to go to nothing but Wesleyan school treats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism and artistic practice should acknowledge the interplay of moral sensibility and aesthetic taste. Beware of claims of 'art for art's sake' that mask personal moral preferences; an ideal critic sees enduring ethics as well as enduring beauty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artist's personal virtues affect reception
rubrics_metrics.description: No man ever preached the impersonality of art so well; no man ever preached the impersonality of art so personally... His talents were many, his virtues, it must be confessed, not many, beyond that kindness to tried friends... outstanding virtues limit themselves chiefly to two admirable ones—courage and an abstract love of good work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The perceived character and virtues of an artist (courage, dedication to good work) influence how their art is received. Claims of impersonality are suspect if the artist's life and disputes dominate public perception; cultivate genuine virtues that sustain artistic endeavour.
